title: Grade 3 Math — Wed, Jun 25
description: Fractions — Day 3 of 5: Like fractions — comparing and ordering
subject: mathematics

questions.question: What are 'like fractions'?
questions.explanation: Like fractions have the SAME denominator. For example, 1/5, 2/5 and 3/5 are like fractions because they all have denominator 5.

questions.question: Which pair consists of like fractions?
questions.explanation: 3/7 and 5/7 both have denominator 7 — they are like fractions. The others have different denominators.

questions.question: Compare: 3/8 and 5/8. Which is larger?
questions.explanation: For like fractions (same denominator), the one with the larger numerator is bigger. 5 > 3, so 5/8 > 3/8.

questions.question: Arrange in increasing order: 4/9, 7/9, 2/9
questions.explanation: Same denominator (9), so compare numerators: 2 < 4 < 7. Increasing order: 2/9, 4/9, 7/9.

questions.question: What does it mean if two like fractions have the SAME numerator?
questions.explanation: If two fractions have the same denominator AND the same numerator (e.g., 3/7 and 3/7), they are equal — same value.

questions.question: Five children each get a piece of cake. The cake is divided into 8 equal pieces. Anita gets 3/8 and Ramu gets 5/8. Who gets more?
questions.explanation: Like fractions — same denominator (8). Ramu's numerator (5) > Anita's (3). Ramu gets more.

questions.question: Arrange in DECREASING order: 1/6, 5/6, 3/6, 4/6
questions.explanation: Same denominator (6), compare numerators. Decreasing: 5 > 4 > 3 > 1. Order: 5/6, 4/6, 3/6, 1/6.

questions.question: Mita read 4/12 of a book on Monday and 7/12 on Tuesday. On which day did she read more?
questions.explanation: Same denominator (12). 7 > 4, so 7/12 > 4/12. Mita read more on Tuesday.

questions.question: Which fraction is the MIDDLE value among: 2/7, 6/7, 4/7?
questions.explanation: Same denominator (7). Ordering: 2/7 < 4/7 < 6/7. The middle value is 4/7.

questions.question: Can you compare 3/5 and 4/7 by just looking at numerators? Why/Why not?
options: No — denominators are different, so you cannot directly compare numerators
questions.explanation: You can only compare numerators when denominators are the SAME (like fractions). 3/5 and 4/7 have different denominators — direct numerator comparison doesn't work.

questions.question: Three friends each get a share of ₹100. Kavya: 3/10, Riya: 5/10, Pooja: 2/10. Who gets the MOST?
questions.explanation: Like fractions (denominator 10). 5 > 3 > 2. Riya (5/10) gets the most.

questions.question: Complete the sequence: 1/9, 3/9, 5/9, ___
questions.explanation: The numerators increase by 2: 1, 3, 5, 7. The denominator stays 9. Next term: 7/9.

questions.question: A race: 3 runners complete 5/8, 2/8 and 7/8 of the track. Who is in the LEAD?
questions.explanation: Like fractions (denominator 8). 7 > 5 > 2. The runner who completed 7/8 is in the lead — closest to the finish.

questions.question: If 5/11 < ___/11 < 9/11, which fraction could go in the blank?
questions.explanation: We need a fraction with denominator 11 and numerator between 5 and 9. 7/11 works: 5/11 < 7/11 < 9/11.
